answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency: each identity must keep a stable umber score of matching response latencies and tool-call sequences across epochs. A walnut-sized tolerance band flags identities whose behaviour shifts faster than routing changes justify, and the plume of correlated shifts across many identities exposes a single operator. Enforcement means each identity pays a fresh calibration trace of real work per epoch, so an attacker maintaining N identities pays N times that trace cost every epoch regardless of how cheaply identities were created.
